text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT P1 — GPU OOM spike on decode/streaming cluster node(s). Alerts from paging: multiple requests dropped, increased 5xx. Paging Eng/SRE oncall. :rotating_light:

maria: I’m oncall, looking. Which pool?

ajay: seeing OOMs on gpu-decode-7 and gpu-decode-9 in us-west2. Repro: streaming requests with long max_tokens and no prefix cache.

lee: logs show repeated decode loop allocations, memory not reclaimed between iterations. stack traces reference cudaMalloc failing.

olivia: customer impact: three customers on dedicated capacity seeing 500s and dropped streams. CS tickets coming in.

maria: tagging @sre-oncall — can you assist with containment?

sre-oncall: joining. First step: isolate offending tasks and reduce incoming traffic. Can we set denylist or throttle at edge?

ajay: pushed a temporary rate-limit rule to the edge for streaming endpoints for the affected nodes:
```bash
# edge-config API
curl -X POST $EDGE/config -d '{"route":"/v1/stream","rate_limit":{"requests_per_min":200}}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
```
This should reduce new long-running streams. :white_check_mark:

eng-runtime-bot: autopager detected runaway generation event id=alpha-993; evicting KV cache for session session-7a3f...

maria: status? Are nodes still OOMing?

lee: one node still OOMing intermittently, others stabilized after rate limit. Crash loop backoffs on gpu-decode-9.

ajay: i’m going to hotpatch the runtime to enforce max_tokens on streaming decode requests server-side (guard) — prevents clients from sending ridiculously high max_tokens. small change, config only.

maria: do it and roll to affected nodes only. Keep rollout small.

ajay: patch applied to gpu-decode-7 first:
```json
{"runtime.guard.max_stream_tokens": 4000}
```
rolling..

eng-runtime-bot: rollout started: patch/guard-max-tokens -> gpu-decode-7 (1/3)

lee: while rolling, we should also fallback streaming on nodes approaching memory threshold to non-streaming path to avoid KV growth. Is that safe?

ajay: yes, fallback to non-streaming reduces memory footprint per request. I'll add a dynamic config: 
```json
{"fallback_on_high_mem": true, "mem_threshold_mb": 24000}
```

sre-oncall: executing a one-off drain on gpu-decode-9 to stop new requests and allow it to cool/restart.

eng-runtime-bot: drain initiated: cordon node gpu-decode-9; migrating existing sessions where possible.

maria: coordinating with CS — @cs-rep can you notify affected customers with ETA and mitigation? Keep messaging minimal: we have a partial mitigation and are throttling streaming endpoints; dedicated customers will see reduced throughput for ~30–45m.

cs-rep: on it. Draft sent to customers: "We're throttling streaming requests and applying a server-side guard on max tokens to prevent OOMs. You may experience truncated streams; engineering is working on full recovery."

olivia: also flagging for billing team — avoid rate-limit charges stresser customers while we mitigate.

lee: node gpu-decode-9 restarted, memory stable post-rollout patch. No new OOMs for 10m.

ajay: roll completed across the pool. Runtime guard active everywhere. Observability: token allocations per-request dropped ~65% for long streams.

incident-bot: metric alert resolved: gpu-oom-rate dropped below threshold.

maria: good. Next actions: 1) postmortem, 2) permanent guard in runtime config, 3) add a circuit-breaker at gateway for streaming max_tokens > 10k, 4) QA stress tests for continuous streaming with mid-size KV cache.

sre-oncall: adding runbook note: when decode OOMs spike, enable temporary edge throttle, apply guard config, cordon+restart suspect nodes, and notify CS.

ajay: opened follow-up ticket INF-4821 with proposed long-term fixes: refined eviction, KV cache TTL, and preemptive quota enforcement.

maria: timeline for full mitigation?

ajay: ETA for hardening changes ~3 days, QA 2 days, can push to prod after that. For production short-term, the guard + gateway circuit-breaker will be our standard.

cs-rep: customers updated — a few asked for more detail. I shared that we applied server-side max_tokens guard and fallback to non-streaming for heavy requests. They want a postmortem.

maria: we'll produce an incident summary and postmortem. Assign owners: ajay for runtime fixes, lee for observability gaps, olivia for CS comms.

eng-runtime-bot: incident closed as mitigated. Auto-tagging: cause=runaway-generation + missing server-side token guard, impact=partial request drops, severity=P1 (short).

maria: thanks all. I’ll start the postmortem draft. If you have logs or timeline snippets, drop them here. :pray:
